qa_pairs.question: How can I determine the amount of Slurm node memory required for an Abaqus simulation?
qa_pairs.answer: An estimate for the total Slurm node memory (`--mem=`) needed to run a simulation fully in RAM can be obtained by examining the Abaqus output `test.dat` file, specifically the "MEMORY TO MINIMIZE I/O" value. Alternatively, for a single node threaded process, one can run the simulation interactively on a compute node and monitor memory use with the `top` or `ps` command, observing the VIRT and RES columns until steady peak memory values are observed.

qa_pairs.question: When configuring Slurm jobs for Abaqus, what do "MEMORY TO MINIMIZE I/O" (MRMIO) and "MINIMUM MEMORY REQUIRED" (MMR) indicate regarding memory allocation?
qa_pairs.answer: "MEMORY TO MINIMIZE I/O" (MRMIO) represents the memory required to minimize I/O operations by running the simulation fully in RAM. To fully satisfy MRMIO, at least the same amount of non-swapped physical memory (RES) must be available. "MINIMUM MEMORY REQUIRED" (MMR) is the absolute lowest RES memory that can be allocated; if RES drops below MMR, Abaqus will terminate due to an Out of Memory (OOM) error. It is generally necessary to slightly over-allocate the requested Slurm node memory (`--mem=`) because RES will typically be less than the virtual memory (VIRT).
